title: Transmission line lengths and stubs
blurb: Explain velocity factor, what shorted and open lines look like at 1/8, 1/4 and 1/2 wavelength, and why open wire beats coax on loss.

E9F01.why: Velocity factor = speed in the line ÷ speed of light in a vacuum. A ratio below 1, about 1 for air.
E9F01.trap: Impedance ratios describe SWR and reflection, not speed.

E9F02.why: The **insulating dielectric** sets how much the wave slows. Air is about 1; plastic is lower.
E9F02.trap: Impedance and length don't change velocity factor.

E9F03.why: Waves travel **more slowly** in the dielectric, so wavelengths are shorter and the line holds more of them than its length suggests.
E9F03.trap: Skin effect isn't what stretches electrical length.

E9F04.why: Shorted at ½ λ: the short repeats every half wavelength, so the generator sees a **very low impedance**.

E9F05.why: Microstrip is a **printed conductor above a ground plane**: a constant-impedance line for microwave circuit boards.

E9F06.why: Half wave = 299.8 ÷ 14.10 ÷ 2 = **10.6 m**. Air-insulated line has VF about 1, so no shortening.
E9F06.trap: 7.0 m is 10.6 × 0.66, the length for solid plastic coax.

E9F07.why: Air and wide spacing give open-wire line **lower loss** than plastic-dielectric coax.

E9F08.why: Foam is mostly air: **lower loss and higher VF**, but a **lower voltage rating**. All three differences apply.

E9F09.why: Shorted at ¼ λ: the short is inverted along the line, so the generator sees a **very high impedance**.

E9F10.why: Shorted and shorter than ¼ λ: **inductive**. At ⅛ λ, X = Z₀ × tan 45° = +jZ₀.

E9F11.why: Open and shorter than ¼ λ: **capacitive**. At ⅛ λ, X = −jZ₀.

E9F12.why: Open at ¼ λ: the open is inverted, so the generator sees a **very low impedance**.
